column1: # gates/build-numbers.tsv - THE REGISTER OF BUILD NUMBERS ALREADY ISSUED.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The build number is the key the whole record hangs on - flags, gate logs, RUN-LOG rows,
# case results, the dashboard and every "shipped at #NNN" claim key off it - and until now it was CHOSEN BY EACH
# RUN from what that run could see. Two runs that could not see each other chose the same one, so "#416" names
# two different trees. Measured from the logs themselves rather than repeated from prose:
#   claude/agents/gatelogs/416-main-all.log     bundle md5 b2ab30ff6784   stamp "#416 - 2026-09-18 14:32 ET"   1916 PASS
#   claude/agents/gatelogs/416-branch-all.log   bundle md5 69b903f2b0ca   stamp "#416 - 2026-09-18 00:18 ET"   1938 PASS
# Both end "GATES GREEN #416". That is why two gate logs collided on a filename, and it is why a flag can
# truthfully say "36 controlled suites at #416" about a tree that does not ship.
# jobs/mint-build-numbers-from-one-place is this file's job; `gates/buildnum.sh` is how you read and write it.
# AND THE COLLISION IS NO LONGER THE INTERESTING HALF. MEASURED 2026-10-01 by build__1790886022489, one
# `git show <sha>:app.js | md5sum` per commit touching app.js on origin/main: of the EIGHT build numbers with an
# app.js commit in this (shallow, 50-commit) clone, FOUR name more than one distinct bundle - #440 three,
# #441 two, #451 three, #452 two. So a number is ambiguous about as often as not, TODAY, with no second build
# line in existence. #439's "three bundles under one stamp" was filed as an anomaly and is the median behaviour
# of any number whose run needed a fix. This count is a LOWER BOUND twice over: it sees only bundles that were
# COMMITTED (intermediate ones replaced in-run never appear - #439 reads 1 here and the job records 3) and only
# back to #439, because the clone is shallow.
# WHAT THE BACKFILL BELOW IS AND IS NOT, AND IT TOOK TWO PASSES. Rows marked `run-log` or `gatelog` came from
# RUN-LOG.md and the committed gate-log filenames; rows marked `git-log` came from a second pass over git. They
# establish ONE fact - THE NUMBER WAS USED - and that is the only fact `check` needs. Their state is `issued`,
# deliberately NOT `shipped`: a shallow clone cannot prove what reached main, and claiming `shipped` for ninety
# builds nobody measured would be the frozen denominator this project keeps paying for. sha, bundleMd5 and
# sourceMd5 are `-` on them because they were not measured, not because they are absent. Rows marked `measured`
# or `build.sh` carry numbers read off the artefact itself.
# THE FIRST PASS WAS SHORT BY 123 NUMBERS AND THREE OF THEM WERE INSIDE THE LIVE RANGE. It read only RUN-LOG.md
# and the gatelog filenames, so it covered #347-#454 with holes, and #444, #445 and #446 READ `free` - the one
# answer this register must never give wrongly - because those runs used the `#NNNrun` form and produced no
# bundle, so neither source saw them. Measured by antagonist B, re-derived and fixed in the same build.
# THE METHOD OF THE SECOND PASS, so it can be re-run rather than trusted: `git log --all --format=%s |
# grep -oE '^#[0-9]{3,4}'` over the 789 reachable commits. A number counts only when a commit SUBJECT STARTS
# with it, i.e. that commit claims it. That discrimination is load-bearing: scanning for #NNN anywhere in a
# subject also returns cross-references such as the #125 in "Friends: cloud functions ... for #125", which was
# never a build number. 214 numbers are self-claimed; 123 were missing here.
# AND IT IS STILL NOT A COMPLETE CENSUS, said plainly: this clone is SHALLOW on HEAD (50 commits) even though
# `git log --all` reaches 789, numbers used before the git history begins cannot appear at all, and a number
# that was minted and never committed anywhere is invisible to every pass. ERRING TOWARD RECORDING IS
# DELIBERATE: a wrongly-recorded number costs one number, and a gap is free, while a wrongly-`free` number is
# the defect this file exists to prevent.
# HOW TO USE IT. `CT_RUNID=<your runId> gates/buildnum.sh mint '<what this build is for>'` takes the next free
# number and records it; then build it. gates/build.sh refuses a number that is NOT THIS RUN'S - not merely one
# this file carries, which is a different and wrong question: asking it that way deadlocked mint-then-build,
# because the `minted` row mint had just written was reason enough to refuse. `gates/buildnum.sh stampable
# '#NNN'` is the predicate build.sh uses; `check` is the broader query, true of any row. CT_RENUM=1 overrides.
# After a successful bundle, build.sh appends a `built` row itself, so every number RESOLVES to the artefacts
# stamped with it - point 2 of the job brief, delivered in a committed file rather than in the stamp; see the
# header of buildnum.sh for why the stamp cannot carry a commit sha and why its own md5 is dearer than it looks.
# A NUMBER IS NEVER REMOVED AND NEVER REUSED. If a number was minted and the run died, it stays `minted` and
# the series moves past it. A gap is free; a reuse is the defect. BUT "A GAP IS FREE" IS A STATEMENT ABOUT COST,
# NOT A CLAIM THAT EVERY GAP IN THIS FILE IS AN UNUSED NUMBER - the first backfill left 123 used numbers absent,
# and the paragraph above says how that was measured and why the census is still incomplete.
# FORMAT: tab-separated.
# number | state (minted|issued|built|shipped|held|abandoned) | sha | bundleMd5 | sourceMd5 |
#   at (ISO-8601 UTC) | mintedBy (runId) | provenance (run-log|gatelog|measured|build.sh|minted) | note
